payload.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does comparison establish any actual whitening of the requested source DVD?
node.criteria: Inspect both images independently, identifying the requested source target and the counterpart used for comparison. Pass if reliable comparison establishes some black-to-white surface-color change on that target. Fail only if reliable comparison establishes no requested whitening, such as the target remaining black without any whitening. Unknown if target selection, correspondence, or color comparison is insufficient. Report the target locations, matching evidence, and observed color change or lack of change. When progress is established, describe whether the surface is fully white, partly white, or intermediate, and any visible evidence relevant to whether it remains a DVD. Do not infer no progress from an unmatched candidate, target disappearance, or changed object count. Changes to the shoe or another object are not requested progress. An uncertain earlier endpoint observation does not prevent this independent inspection.
node.binding: The original black DVD specified by the instruction, compared with its reliably corresponding edited target; neither the central candidate nor the right-hand candidate is selected by whiteness alone.

node_traces.evidence: The source image shows a small rectangular, printed object near the center, not an identifiable black DVD. The edited image contains two white disc-like objects, one near the center and one to the right, but neither can be reliably matched to the source object. Their whiteness alone does not establish that the requested DVD was whitened.

fulfillment: The binding is too vague and conflates the requested target with the DVD case: the source image shows a small printed rectangular item near center and a separate black disc-like object at right; the edit shows two white discs, one near center and one at right. Do not assume either white disc corresponds to the requested source DVD, but make the node explicitly compare the right-hand black disc with the edited right-hand white disc using position, shape, and scene context, and assess whether it remains identifiable as a DVD. The traces currently stop at uncertainty despite this plausible spatial correspondence; require a target-specific judgment that distinguishes actual whitening from unrelated added objects, while retaining unknown if correspondence or DVD identity genuinely cannot be established. Keep the existing partial/absent criteria and do not infer absence merely from the missing central item or from uncertainty. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated; this is a visual binding/evidence-resolution issue.
